**Step 1: Asymptotic analysis of the numerator.**

$$\ln(2n^7+13) = \ln\!\big(n^7(2+13/n^7)\big) = 7\ln n + \ln 2 + O(n^{-7})$$

So $\ln(2n^7+13) = 7\ln n\,(1+o(1))$, and

$$\ln^5(2n^7+13) = 7^5\ln^5 n\,(1+o(1)) = 16807\,\ln^5 n\,(1+o(1)).$$

Since $|10\sin n|\le 10 = o(\ln^5 n)$, the numerator is

$$\ln^5(2n^7+13)+10\sin n = 16807\,\ln^5 n\,(1+o(1)).$$

**Step 2: Asymptotic analysis of the denominator.**

$$\ln\!\big(n^{7/8}+2\sqrt{n}-1\big) = \ln\!\big(n^{7/8}(1+2n^{-3/8}-n^{-7/8})\big) = \tfrac{7}{8}\ln n + O(n^{-3/8}) = \tfrac{7}{8}\ln n\,(1+o(1)),$$

so $\ln^6(n^{7/8}+2\sqrt{n}-1) = \left(\frac{7}{8}\right)^6\ln^6 n\,(1+o(1)) = \frac{7^6}{8^6}\ln^6 n\,(1+o(1)).$

For the inner logarithm: $\ln(n+(-1)^n) = \ln n + O(1/n) = \ln n\,(1+o(1))$, hence

$$\ln\!\big(\ln(n+(-1)^n)\big) = \ln(\ln n + O(1/n)) = \ln(\ln n)\,(1+o(1)).$$

Combining, the denominator is

$$n\cdot\frac{7^6}{8^6}\ln^6 n\cdot\ln(\ln n)\cdot(1+o(1)).$$

**Step 3: Asymptotic form of the general term.**

$$a_n = \frac{16807\,\ln^5 n\,(1+o(1))}{n\cdot\frac{7^6}{8^6}\ln^6 n\cdot\ln(\ln n)\cdot(1+o(1))} = \frac{7^5\cdot 8^6}{7^6}\cdot\frac{1}{n\ln n\,\ln(\ln n)}\,(1+o(1)) = \frac{8^6}{7}\cdot\frac{1}{n\ln n\,\ln(\ln n)}\,(1+o(1)).$$

That is,

$$a_n \sim \frac{262144}{7}\cdot\frac{1}{n\ln n\,\ln(\ln n)}.$$

**Step 4: Divergence by the integral test.**

The comparison series $\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge 3}\frac{1}{n\ln n\,\ln(\ln n)}$ diverges, since

$$\int_3^{\infty}\frac{dx}{x\ln x\,\ln(\ln x)} = \Big[\ln(\ln(\ln x))\Big]_3^{\infty} = +\infty.$$

**Step 5: Conclusion via the limit comparison test.**

Since $a_n \sim \frac{262144}{7}\cdot\frac{1}{n\ln n\,\ln(\ln n)}$ with $\frac{262144}{7}>0$, and the comparison series diverges, the given series **diverges**.
